content: 1. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate extra strength tablets should be chewed, with a dosage of 2-4 tablets taken orally every 6 hours as needed. Do not exceed 16 tablets per day. 2. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate extra strength suspension should be taken in a dose of 15-30 mL orally every 6 hours as needed. Do not exceed 80 mL per day. 3. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate regular strength suspension should be taken in a dose of 15-30 mL orally every 6 hours as needed. Do not exceed 120 mL per day. 4. The safety and efficacy of aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate have not been established. 5. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of raltegravir by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The combination is contraindicated and not recommended, even with dose separation. 6. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to reduced plasma concentrations. Administer atazanavir 2 hours before or 1 hour after these medications. 7. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Baloxavir may bind to polyvalent cations, reducing absorption. Studies in monkeys showed significant decreases in plasma levels when coadministered with calcium, aluminum, or iron. Human studies have not been conducted. 8. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of dolutegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Administer dolutegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking medications containing polyvalent cations. 9. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, administer infigratinib 2 hours before and after the antacid. 10. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the bioavailability of misoprostol acid through an unknown mechanism. Magnesium-containing antacids may exacerbate misoprostol-induced diarrhea. If an antacid is needed, use one containing aluminum or calcium. 11. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining pazopanib with drugs that raise gastric pH. Short-acting antacids may be used instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) or H2 antagonists, but separate antacid and pazopanib dosing by several hours. 12. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of ponatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, administer sotorasib 4 hours before or 10 hours after the antacid. 14. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of bictegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Bictegravir can be taken under fasting conditions 2 hours before antacids containing aluminum, magnesium, or calcium. Routine administration of bictegravir simultaneously with, or 2 hours after, such antacids is not recommended. 15. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent. Coadministration with drugs that increase gastric pH may cause premature dissolution, potentially affecting release properties and absorption in the duodenum. 16. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of cabotegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Administer antacid products at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after taking oral cabotegravir. 17. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that alter upper gastrointestinal tract pH (e.g., PPIs, H2-blockers, antacids) may decrease dabrafenib solubility and reduce its bioavailability. 18. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels of deferiprone by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Deferiprone may bind to polyvalent cations (e.g., iron, aluminum, zinc). Separate administration by at least 4 hours between deferiprone and other medications (e.g., antacids) or supplements containing these cations. 19. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration from antacids by 2 hours. 20. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate increases the levels of ethambutol by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid administering aluminum hydroxide-containing antacids for at least 4 hours following an ethambutol dose. 21. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by altering solubility. Use caution and monitor closely. Ledipasvir solubility decreases as pH increases. Drugs that increase gastric pH are expected to reduce ledipasvir levels. Separate antacid and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir administration by 4 hours. 22. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Avoid this interaction by administering antacids 2 hours after or 2 hours before nilotinib. 23. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair absorption of tetracyclines, reducing efficacy. Separate dosing of tetracyclines from these products. 24. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Separate pexidartinib administration by 2 hours before or after taking a locally-acting antacid. 25. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels of rifampin by reducing absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. Concomitant antacid administration may reduce rifampin absorption. Daily doses of rifampin should be given at least 1 hour before antacid ingestion. 26. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels of riociguat by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by at least 1 hour. 27. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair absorption of tetracyclines, reducing efficacy. Separate dosing of tetracyclines from these products. 28. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases (practically insoluble at pH >5). Separate administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir from antacids by at least 4 hours. 29. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of vismodegib by altering solubility. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that increase gastric pH alter vismodegib solubility, reducing bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown.
